answer: Ownership is rented, not granted. Each seat carries a self-assessed value posted in a public quartz ledger, and its holder pays the treasury a continuous tax on that figure every epoch. Anyone may buy the seat outright at exactly that price, with no consent asked, so under-valuing a chair invites a raven to take it cheaply and values must stay honest. A surtax climbs with the number of seats one holder owns, and every chair stays exposed to piecemeal buyout, which no proxy or shell keeps off the block. The island of honest holders grows slowly, each paying a small rent for its single chair.
